item.title: Open, Closed, and Short Circuits in a Three-Bulb Circuit
item.stimulus:
An ideal battery has a positive terminal P and a negative terminal N. The circuit is connected as follows.
- Bulb 1 connects terminal P to junction B.
- Bulb 2 connects junction B to junction C.
- Switch S also connects junction B directly to junction C, giving a second path from B to C that contains nothing except the switch.
- A wire connects junction C to terminal N.
- Bulb 3 connects terminal P to point D, and switch T connects point D to terminal N.

All wires and closed switches have negligible resistance. A bulb is lit only when charge flows through it.

parts.prompt: Both switches are open. State which bulbs are lit and which are unlit. Justify your answer in terms of closed and open circuits.

criteria.text: States that bulbs 1 and 2 are lit because the path P → bulb 1 → B → bulb 2 → C → N is a closed loop through the battery.
criteria.evidence: Response identifies bulbs 1 and 2 as lit and describes the closed path from the battery through bulb 1 and bulb 2 back to the battery.
criteria.fix: Trace each bulb's path from one battery terminal to the other; a bulb lights only if that path forms a complete loop.

criteria.text: States that bulb 3 is unlit because open switch T breaks its only path back to the battery, so it is in an open circuit.
criteria.evidence: Response identifies bulb 3 as unlit and explains that charge cannot flow through it because switch T is open.
criteria.fix: Check every switch along a bulb's path; one open switch makes that path an open circuit with no charge flow.

parts.prompt: Switch S is closed while switch T stays open. State whether bulb 2 is lit, and explain using the idea of a short circuit.

criteria.text: States that bulb 2 is unlit because closed switch S lets charge flow from B to C with no change in electric potential (a short circuit), so the potential difference across bulb 2 is zero and no charge flows through it.
criteria.evidence: Response says bulb 2 goes out and explains that the switch path from B to C has no potential difference, so bulb 2, connected between the same two points, has none either.
criteria.fix: When a wire or closed switch joins a bulb's two ends, the bulb has zero potential difference across it; say so explicitly.

parts.prompt: Both switches are now closed. State whether bulb 3 is lit. Then identify two different closed loops that both contain the battery, listing the circuit elements each loop passes through.

criteria.text: States that bulb 3 is lit because closing T completes the closed loop P → bulb 3 → D → switch T → N.
criteria.evidence: Response says bulb 3 is lit and identifies the now-complete path through bulb 3 and switch T back to the battery.
criteria.fix: After a switch closes, retrace the bulb's path to the battery and confirm it now forms a complete loop.

criteria.text: Identifies two valid closed loops containing the battery, chosen from: battery–bulb 1–switch S; battery–bulb 3–switch T; battery–bulb 1–bulb 2.
criteria.evidence: Response lists two of these three loops by their elements, each starting and ending at the battery, showing the battery belongs to more than one loop.
criteria.fix: Start at a battery terminal, follow connected elements without retracing, and stop when you return to the other terminal; repeat along a different route.

item.model_answer:
(a) Bulbs 1 and 2 are lit. The path P → bulb 1 → B → bulb 2 → C → N is a closed loop through the battery, so charge can flow through both bulbs. Switch S is open, so the only path from B to C is through bulb 2.
Bulb 3 is unlit. Its only path back to the battery goes through switch T, which is open, so that path is an open circuit and no charge can flow through bulb 3.

(b) Bulb 2 is unlit. Closing S gives charge a path from B to C through the switch alone, with no change in electric potential; this is a short circuit across bulb 2. Because bulb 2 is connected between the same points B and C, the potential difference across it is zero, so no charge flows through it and it does not light.

(c) Bulb 3 is lit, because closing T completes the closed loop P → bulb 3 → D → switch T → N.
Two closed loops that contain the battery:
Loop 1: battery (P) → bulb 1 → B → switch S → C → battery (N).
Loop 2: battery (P) → bulb 3 → D → switch T → battery (N).
The battery is part of both loops.
